lemmas.proof_markdown: Because $(v_M,u_M)$ is a basis, the affine change from $(T,S)$ to $(X,Y)$ is invertible, and its inverse expresses $T$ and $S$ as affine-linear polynomials in $X$ and $Y$. The inverse third coordinate is $W=Z-P_M(T)$. Since $\deg P_M\le d$, both the substitution and its inverse preserve the filtration with weights $(1,1,d)$. Setting $S=W=0$ gives $(X,Y)=b_M+Tv_M$ and $Z=P_M(T)$, so the lifted graph ideal becomes $(S,W)$. No division by a derivative or factorial is involved.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime, let $100<d<p$, let $s\ge 1$ and $d\le D<p$, and let $M(t)=b_M+tv_M$ be an affine line in $\mathbb F_p^2$ with a polynomial $P_M\in\mathbb F_p[T]$ satisfying $\deg P_M\le d$. Choose $u_M\in\mathbb F_p^2$ such that $(v_M,u_M)$ is a basis. Give $T$ and $S$ weight $1$ and $W$ weight $d$. Then

$$
(X,Y)=b_M+Tv_M+Su_M,\qquad Z=P_M(T)+W
$$

defines a filtered polynomial isomorphism between $\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ and $\mathbb F_p[T,S,W]$. Under this isomorphism, the defining ideal $I_M$ of the lifted graph of $P_M$ is $(S,W)$.
lemmas.title: Adapted normal coordinates

lemmas.proof_markdown:
By the filtered coordinate isomorphism, every $A\in V_D$ has a unique expansion

$$
A=\sum_{a,b\ge 0}c_{a,b}(T)S^aW^b,
$$

where $\deg c_{a,b}\le D-a-db$. Membership in $(S,W)^s$ is equivalent to $c_{a,b}=0$ whenever $a+b<s$. For each such pair, equating the coefficients of $T$ gives exactly $\max\{D-a-db+1,0\}$ independent scalar conditions. The corresponding residue classes of the monomials $T^iS^aW^b$ form a basis of the quotient by $(S,W)^s$, proving the one-line codimension formula. For $n$ lines, the rank of the combined system is at most the sum of the individual codimensions, namely $nC_s(D,d)$; dependencies between constraints from different lines can only reduce this rank.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime, let $100<d<p$, let $s\ge 1$ and $d\le D<p$, and let $V_D\subseteq\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ be the space of polynomials of weighted degree at most $D$ for weights $(1,1,d)$. For a lifted line-graph ideal $I_M$, define

$$
C_s(D,d)=\sum_{\substack{a,b\ge 0\\a+b<s}}\max\{D-a-db+1,0\}.
$$

Then $V_D\cap I_M^s$ has codimension exactly $C_s(D,d)$ in $V_D$. If $\mathcal R$ consists of $n$ distinct lifted line graphs, then the simultaneous conditions $A\in I_M^s$ for all $M\in\mathcal R$ impose at most $nC_s(D,d)$ homogeneous linear equations on $V_D$.
lemmas.title: Normal-jet codimension

lemmas.proof_markdown: For a fixed exponent $j$ of $Z$, the admissible monomials in $X$ and $Y$ have total degree at most $D-dj$ and therefore number $\binom{D-dj+2}{2}$. Summing over $0\le j\le\lfloor D/d\rfloor$ gives $\dim V_D=N_d(D)$. The common order-$s$ conditions have rank at most $nC_s(D,d)$. Thus $N_d(D)>nC_s(D,d)$ leaves a positive-dimensional kernel, which contains a nonzero common interpolant.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime, let $100<d<p$, let $s\ge 1$ and $d\le D<p$, and let $\mathcal R$ consist of $n$ distinct affine lines equipped with polynomials of degree at most $d$. Define

$$
N_d(D)=\sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor D/d\rfloor}\binom{D-dj+2}{2}.
$$

If $N_d(D)>nC_s(D,d)$, then there exists a nonzero polynomial $A\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ of weighted degree at most $D$ such that $A\in I_M^s$ for every $M\in\mathcal R$.
lemmas.title: Jet interpolation

lemmas.proof_markdown: In coordinates adapted to $M$, a polynomial independent of $Z$ is also independent of $W$. Its membership in $(S,W)^s$ therefore forces divisibility by $S^s$. Since $S$ is a nonzero scalar multiple of the line equation $\ell_M$, the factor $\ell_M^s$ divides $A$. The equations of distinct affine lines are pairwise nonassociate prime linear polynomials, so their product to the $s$-th power divides $A$. As $A$ is independent of $Z$, its ordinary degree equals its weighted degree and is at most $D$. Hence $D\ge sn$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime, let $100<d<p$, let $s\ge 1$ and $d\le D<p$, and let $\mathcal R$ consist of $n$ distinct affine lines. Let $A\ne 0$ have weighted degree at most $D$ and satisfy $A\in I_M^s$ for every $M\in\mathcal R$. For each $M\in\mathcal R$, let $\ell_M$ be a nonzero affine-linear equation defining $M$. If $A$ is independent of $Z$, then

$$
\prod_{M\in\mathcal R}\ell_M^s\mid A
$$

and $D\ge sn$. Consequently, if $D<sn$, then $A$ depends on $Z$.
lemmas.title: Line-factor divisibility

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Set $z=\deg_Z A$ and suppose $z<s$. After replacing $Z$ by $P_M(T)+W$, the degree in $W$ remains $z$. Membership in $(S,W)^s$ forces the coefficient of $W^j$ to be divisible by $S^{s-j}$ for every $0\le j\le z$. Hence every coefficient is divisible by $S^{s-z}$, so $\ell_M^{s-z}$ divides $A$ for every $M\in\mathcal R$. Distinctness of the lines then gives

$$
\prod_{M\in\mathcal R}\ell_M^{s-z}\mid A.
$$

If $n>D$, the product has weighted degree $n(s-z)>D$, contradicting $A\ne0$. Therefore $z\ge s$. A term with $Z$-degree $z$ has weighted degree at least $dz$, so $D\ge dz\ge sd$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime, let $100<d<p$, let $s\ge 1$ and $d\le D<p$, and let $\mathcal R$ consist of $n$ distinct affine lines. Let $A\ne0$ have weighted degree at most $D$ and satisfy $A\in I_M^s$ for every $M\in\mathcal R$. If $n>D$, then

$$
\deg_Z A\ge s
$$

and $D\ge sd$.
lemmas.title: Primitive degree cost

lemmas.proof_markdown: Write the leading $Z$-term of $A$ as $a_z(X,Y)Z^z$, where $z\ge1$ and $a_z\ne0$. Weighted degree at most $D$ gives $dz\le D<p$, and hence $1\le z<p$. Thus $z$ is nonzero in $\mathbb F_p$, so the leading term $z a_z(X,Y)Z^{z-1}$ survives formal differentiation. Therefore $A_Z\ne0$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime, let $100<d<p$, and let $d\le D<p$. If a polynomial $A\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ has weighted degree at most $D$ for weights $(1,1,d)$ and depends on $Z$, then its formal derivative satisfies

$$
A_Z=\frac{\partial A}{\partial Z}\ne0.
$$
lemmas.title: Formal derivative

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Use coordinates adapted to $M$. Because $L$ and $M$ are distinct and meet at the indicated point, $S_M(L(t))$ is a nonzero affine-linear polynomial with a simple zero at $t_0$. Moreover,

$$
W_M(L(t),P_L(t))=P_L(t)-P_M(T_M(L(t)))
$$

vanishes at $t_0$ by compatibility of the two labels. Thus both normal generators pull back to polynomials divisible by $t-t_0$. Every term belonging to $(S_M,W_M)^s$ consequently pulls back to a multiple of $(t-t_0)^s$. No derivative or factorial is divided by.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime, let $100<d<p$, let $s\ge1$ and $d\le D<p$, and let $M$ and $L$ be distinct affine lines with parameterizations $M(r)$ and $L(t)$. Let $P_M$ and $P_L$ have degree at most $d$. Suppose that

$$
L(t_0)=M(r_0),\qquad P_L(t_0)=P_M(r_0).
$$

If $A$ has weighted degree at most $D$ and $A\in I_M^s$, then

$$
(t-t_0)^s\mid A(L(t),P_L(t)).
$$
lemmas.title: Transverse root multiplicity

lemmas.proof_markdown:
Each compatible intersection supplies the divisibility $(t-t_i)^s\mid g_L(t)$ by the transverse-root entry. The parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_h$ are distinct, so these factors are pairwise coprime and

$$
\prod_{i=1}^h(t-t_i)^s\mid g_L(t).
$$

Substituting the affine coordinates of $L(t)$ and the degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial $P_L(t)$ into a polynomial of weighted degree at most $D$ gives $\deg g_L\le D$. If $sh>D$, a nonzero $g_L$ cannot have the displayed divisor. Hence $g_L=0$.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime, let $100<d<p$, let $s\ge1$ and $d\le D<p$, and let $\mathcal R$ consist of distinct affine lines equipped with polynomials of degree at most $d$. Let $A$ have weighted degree at most $D$ and satisfy $A\in I_M^s$ for every $M\in\mathcal R$. Let $L$ be an affine line with a polynomial $P_L$ of degree at most $d$. Suppose there are distinct parameters $t_1,\ldots,t_h$ and, for each $i$, a line $M_i\in\mathcal R$ with $M_i\ne L$ and a parameter $r_i$ such that

$$
L(t_i)=M_i(r_i),\qquad P_L(t_i)=P_{M_i}(r_i).
$$

If $sh>D$, then

$$
A(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0.
$$
lemmas.title: Target-line transfer

lemmas.proof_markdown:
For any $D\ge d$, consider the $Z$-levels $0\le j\le\lfloor D/(2d)\rfloor$. There are more than $D/(2d)$ such levels, and each has $D-dj\ge D/2$, so it contains more than $D^2/8$ admissible monomials in $X$ and $Y$. Consequently,

$$
N_d(D)>\frac{D^3}{16d}.
$$

Also,

$$
C_s(D,d)\le\binom{s+1}{2}(D+1)\le s(s+1)D.
$$

The definition of $D_0$ gives

$$
D_0^2>16dns(s+1),
$$

and therefore $N_d(D_0)>nC_s(D_0,d)$. Homogeneous linear algebra yields a nonzero common interpolant of weighted degree at most $D_0$. Finally, $D_0<sh$ permits target-line transfer by multiplicity root counting.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime, let $100<d<p$, let $n\ge1$ and $s\ge1$, and let $\mathcal R$ consist of $n$ distinct affine lines equipped with polynomials of degree at most $d$. Define

$$
D_0=\left\lfloor4\sqrt{dns(s+1)}\right\rfloor+1.
$$

If $d\le D_0<p$, then there exists a nonzero polynomial $A$ of weighted degree at most $D_0$ satisfying $A\in I_M^s$ for every $M\in\mathcal R$. If, in addition, $D_0<sh$, then every target line having $h$ distinct compatible intersections with members of $\mathcal R$ satisfies

$$
A(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0.
$$
lemmas.title: Explicit degree choice

lemmas.proof_markdown:
The dimension inequality supplies a nonzero common interpolant. Since $n>D$, the primitive degree entry gives $D\ge sd$. Hence every summand in $C_s(D,d)$ is active, and direct summation gives

$$
C_s(D,d)=\binom{s+1}{2}(D+1)-(d+1)\binom{s+1}{3}\ge\frac{s^2D}{6}.
$$

For $D\ge d>100$, the monomial count also satisfies

$$
N_d(D)\le\frac{2D^3}{d}.
$$

Therefore $N_d(D)>nC_s(D,d)$ implies

$$
\frac{2D^3}{d}>\frac{ns^2D}{6},
$$

and thus

$$
D^2>\frac{dns^2}{12}.
$$

The transfer condition $sh>D$ now yields

$$
h^2>\frac{D^2}{s^2}>\frac{dn}{12}.
$$

If $n=\Theta(p/\varepsilon)$ and $h=\Theta(\varepsilon p)$, substitution into this inequality gives $\varepsilon^2p^2=\Omega(dp/\varepsilon)$, equivalently $\varepsilon^3=\Omega(d/p)$. The multiplicity parameter $s$ cancels.
lemmas.statement_markdown:
Let $p$ be prime, let $100<d<p$, let $s\ge1$ and $d\le D<p$, and let $\mathcal R$ consist of $n$ distinct affine lines equipped with polynomials of degree at most $d$. Define

$$
N_d(D)=\sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor D/d\rfloor}\binom{D-dj+2}{2},\qquad C_s(D,d)=\sum_{\substack{a,b\ge0\\a+b<s}}\max\{D-a-db+1,0\}.
$$

Suppose that

$$
n>D,\qquad N_d(D)>nC_s(D,d),\qquad sh>D.
$$

Then

$$
h^2>\frac{dn}{12}.
$$

If, along a parameter family with $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$, one additionally has $n=\Theta(p/\varepsilon)$ and $h=\Theta(\varepsilon p)$, then

$$
\varepsilon^3=\Omega\!\left(\frac{d}{p}\right).
$$
lemmas.title: Rank-blind barrier
